title: token-cost-symphony-and-latency-lens
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: long-tail cost and transient latency patterns were hard to correlate at token granularity across services. This PR introduces a small-footprint cross-service enrichment flow ("token-cost-symphony") plus a new visualization component ("latency-lens") to help SREs and engineers quickly surface cost/latency relationships per invocation phase.

What this changes: 1) Telemetry schema: adds a cost_fingerprint tag and a phase_duration histogram to the v2 telemetry stream. 2) Span enrichment: lightweight in-path enricher attaches cost_fingerprint and token_phase tags using an LRU KV to avoid extra DB calls. 3) Sampler: phase-aware reservoir sampler (configurable weight by phase) to keep high-fidelity traces for rare high-cost/latency combinations. 4) Dashboards: latency-lens panel with micro-heatmap (latency vs token-offset) and a cost-symphony sparkline that aggregates cost by phase. 5) Playbook & Docs: rollout steps, alert tuning guidance, and incident runbook snippets.

Design notes: the cost_fingerprint is a 8-byte hex string computed deterministically from model, quantization profile, token-shape (prompt + completion length), and kernel-selection metadata. It is intentionally compact to keep cardinality low while enabling joins across logs, metrics, and traces. The phase_duration histogram uses a 10-bin fixed slabting chosen to emphasize tail behavior without blowing up storage. Enrichment is best-effort — when the in-path enricher cannot compute a fingerprint (e.g., missing metadata), spans are left untouched to avoid inflating error rates.

Rollout plan: staged canary across 3 clusters (5%/25%/100%) controlled via config flag. Sampler defaults to 0.1% globally and 2.5% for invocations with >50ms kernel stalls. Dashboards are added to the "Observability/Incidents" folder and hidden by default; we invited SREs for initial feedback.

Testing: unit tests for fingerprint generation and sampler statistics; e2e tests exercising collector pipeline and dashboard rendering in the dev stack. Performance microbenchmarks show <1.2% p95 tail increase in request latency when enrichment is enabled (measured on a small dedicated canary pool).

Migration/backwards compatibility: telemetry v2 path accepts both presence and absence of cost_fingerprint. Alert rules that previously relied on raw token cost should continue to work; we added example rewrites in the playbook to switch to phase-aware alerting.

Checklist: 
- [x] Telemetry schema change and migration notes
- [x] Span enrichers implemented with fallback path
- [x] Sampler and config knobs exposed
- [x] Dashboard JSON and panel tests
- [x] Docs and rollout playbook

Related work: complements ENG-4720 (prefix warmup traces) and ENG-4903 (adaptive batching instrumentation). Support case SUP-319 reported noisy SLOs for a customer (stacktrace attached) which motivated the focused phase decomposition and sampler heuristics.

review_comments: Ben Huang: Can we make sure the fingerprint algorithm is stable across binary upgrades? If kernels change naming, we need a deterministic mapping. -> Author replied: We added a kernel-mapping table in code and a migration note in docs. The mapping is explicitly versioned to avoid surprises.

Marta Ruiz: The reservoir sampler looks good but we should expose per-tenant overrides for enterprise customers. -> Author replied: Added tenant-level config hooks and documented the default quotas/limits.

Liam O'Connor: Dashboard looks busy; can we add a condensed single-line sparkline for pager duty views? -> Author replied: Added a compact sparkline panel and a query param to hide the micro-heatmap for on-call views.
release_notes: Introduce compact cost_fingerprint and latency-lens dashboard to correlate token-level cost and latency by invocation phase. Includes phase-aware sampler and rollout playbook. No breaking changes; telemetry v2 accepts optional fingerprint.
